candidates.change_summary: Remove the nonReentrant_ modifier from addToBalance so reentrant calls can add to balances, changing stored userBalance values.
Move the statement locked_ = false before the _; placeholder so the lock is released during the guarded function's execution, disabling the reentrancy protection and enabling reentrant state changes.
Return a hardcoded zero instead of the stored user balance.
Add one to the returned balance so it differs from the stored value.
Overwrite the balance with msg.value instead of adding to it, so prior balance is lost.
Delete the balance update so sent Ether is never credited.
Replace addition with subtraction so deposits decrease the recorded balance.
Remove the nonReentrant_ modifier, allowing reentrant addToBalance calls (behavior change in reentrancy scenarios).
Delete the reset of locked_ after the function body so the guard never unlocks and subsequent calls revert.
Change the guard check to require(locked_) so normal (first) calls revert.
Delete the statement 'userBalance[msg.sender] = 0;' so the caller's balance is never reset after withdrawal.
Move 'userBalance[msg.sender] = 0;' to before the external call so the balance is zeroed prior to sending funds.
Remove the nonReentrant_ modifier from withdrawBalance, allowing reentrancy during the external call.
Delete 'locked_ = false;' so the lock is never released and any later nonReentrant_ call reverts.
Delete the statement `userBalance[msg.sender] = 0;` so the caller's balance is never cleared after withdrawal.
Move the statement `userBalance[msg.sender] = 0;` to before the external call, so a reentrant addToBalance during the call is not wiped out.
Delete `locked_ = false;` so the lock is never released after the first protected call, making all subsequent withdrawBalance calls revert and leaving balances unzeroed.
Delete `require(!locked_);` so the reentrancy guard is disabled, allowing a reentrant addToBalance during the ETH call whose credit is then erased by the outer zeroing.
